Name: Wiki Help :: Function Calling Convention
Description: Outlines the syntax and formatting for calling wiki functions.
Body:
@@HideFooterComments @@HideFooterLastModified @@protect(true)
##title @@Tags(Official-Help, Help, Wiki, Official)
##toc

==Overview
Functions are macros which are embedded in the wiki text that when called can alter the text of the wikipage, add meta-data, modify formatting, search, etc. Whitespace before and after the delimiters does not affect the values being passed.


==Parameters
Parameters are the values that are passed to functions which dictate their behavior. When multiple parameters are being passed to a function, they must be delimited by a comma !!(,)!! symbol.


**Parameters come in three varieties:**
{{Bullets
**Required**
>When a function has required parameters, they must be passed, or an error will occur. If a function has required parameters, they will **always** the first parameters.
>Required parameters **cannot** come after optional parameters.
**Optional**
>If a function has optional parameters, they do not need to be specified in the function call.
>If a function has both optional and required parameters, the optional parameters will always come after the required.
>Optional parameters have default values which are used when the parameter is not passed.
**Infinite**
>Infinite parameters are rather special but are used quite frequently in this wiki.
>Infinite parameters allow you to pass many values to a function. For example, if you were to call a function that takes "search terms" as a parameter, you'd likely want to add more than one term. Infinite parameters allow you to do just that.
>Infinite parameters can be either optional or required.
>All parameters that come after an infinite parameter will **always** be optional.
>All parameters that come after an infinite parameter **must** be passed by name.
}}


===Basic function call with infinite parameter
In this example, you can see that we are calling the !!TextList()!! function and passing it several search terms. We are able to pass as many as we like because the first parameter of the !!TextList()!! function is an infinite parameter.

{{Callout(Primary, Example)
#{    ##TextList(wiki, help, official)    }#
}}

===Named optional parameters
Again, in this example, you can see that we are calling the !!TextList()!! function and passing it several search terms - but we also want to now pass the !!top!! parameter to limit the number of pages the function will return. As discussed previously, if the optional parameter comes after an infinite parameter, then we must pass the optional parameter by name.


Passing an optional parameter by name is as simple as placing a colon before the name of the parameter, followed by an equal sign and then the value we want to pass. See below that the !!:top=5!! parameter is being passed by name:

{{Callout(Primary, Example)
#{    ##TextList(wiki, help, official , :top=5)    }#
}}

Additionally if we want to pass the view parameter, we'd add a !!(,)!! symbol to denote a new parameter and then specify the colon, parameter name and value just as before: !!:view=List!!:

{{Callout(Primary, Example)
#{    ##TextList(wiki, help, official , :top=5, :view=List)    }#
}}

==Discrete parameters
Some functions take parameters that expect specific values from a discrete set of values to be passed. If you pass an invalid parameter value, an error will occur.


==Parameter data types 
Parameters are constrained to one of several data types:
{{Bullets
**String**

If you also need to include a double quote in your text, you can escape with a backslash (\). For example !!"This \"is\" a test"!!.
**Integer**
> Non-decimal numeric values between -2,000,000,000 and +2,000,000,000
**Double**
> Decimal numeric values between. Both precise and large.
}}

==Installing on Windows
===Video installation walk-through on YouTube

{{Alert(Primary, ".NET Version")
Note that these instructions may reference an older version of .NET, but TightWiki is generally built against the most current version of .NET, so adjust these instructions accordingly.


For example, this wiki is running on version **##DotNetVersion()**
}}


A quick walkthrough showing how to install your own copy of TightWiki on Windows 2022 server, detailing installing and configuring IIS, installing the ASP.NET core hosting bundle, applying permission for the TightWiki files and finally changing the default TightWiki password. This video deviates a bit from the instructions below, but much of it is applicable.

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/4YIo7K7Yq5A?si=SmCmdRdaFtTfoKid" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe>


===Download and install the ASP.NET Core Runtime 10.0.
There are several downloads available, but you are looking for the **Hosting Bundle** for windows at: [[https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/10.0]]

Download and install on your server.

##Image(Hosting Bundle for Windows.png)


===Create user
It is advisable to create a user for the wiki site to run under. This can be a local user or an active directory user. Here we will use a local account called //mytightwiki_com//.

##Image(Create Windows User.png)


===Create directory
Create a directory to house the TightWiki website files. Here we will use //C:\inetpub\MyTightWiki//

##Image(Create Directory.png)


===Extract files
Download the latest version of TightWiki.zip and extract it to the new directory we just created Here we are using 7-zip to extract to //C:\inetpub\MyTightWiki//.

The directory //C:\inetpub\MyTightWiki// should now contain two additional directories which were extracted from the zip file: //Site// and //Data//. The //Site// directory contains the website files while the //Data// directory contains the SQLite database files.

##Image(Extract TightWiki.png)


===Assign permissions
Ensure that the account you created (//mytightwiki_com//) has read access to //Site// and read and write access to //Data//.


===Create IIS site
Open //Internet Information Services (IIS) Manager// and add a new site. 

##Image(IIS Add Site.png)


===Configure the IIS site
Once you have clicked //Add website// on the previous step, it is time to configure the site. Here we will call the site //MyTightWiki// and select the directory where we previously extracted the TightWiki.zip files (//C:\inetpub\MyTightWiki//).
##Image(Configure IIS Site.png)


===Configure the site user
IIS will access your server using the user which we enter here on the //Add website// dialog. Here you will enter the username and password that we created on step 2 that we called //mytightwiki_com//.

##Image(IIS Site User.png)


===Configure database location
You should not have to modify this, but the location of the SQLite database files is located in the //Site\appsettings.json// file.

##Image(Database Config.png)

Name: Wiki Help :: Links
Description: Linking between wiki pages and external content.
Body:
@@HideFooterComments @@HideFooterLastModified @@protect(true)
##title @@Tags(Official-Help, Help, Wiki, Official)
##toc

==Overview
Linking allows you to create links between internal wiki pages and also external content. When you create a link, clicking on the link will take you to the page which is being linked. If the page does not exist, then the page will be created when you click the link to the page.

All links are enclosed in two sets of square brackets and their parts are separated by commas, in this order:
{{Bullets
The page name or URL being linked to.
Optionally, the link text or an image (prefixed with !!image:!!).
Optionally, when an image is used, a number which is the scale of the image as a percentage.
Optionally, any number of options, such as !!target:!!, in any order.
}}


===Basic links
Basic links are created by enclosing text inside of two sets of square brackets. The text will be the name of the page that you are linking to.
For example, this would be a link to the home page: !!#{[[Home]]}#!! and it would look like this [[::Home]].


===Custom text links
In addition to the basic link above, you can specify custom text after a comma.

For example, this would be a link to the home page with custom text: !!#{[[Home, Take me home!]]}#!! and it would look like this [[::Home, Take me home!]].


===External links
Links to other sites are created the same way, using a URL starting with !!http://!! or !!https://!! in place of the page name.

For example: !!#{[[https://github.com/NTDLS/TightWiki, TightWiki on GitHub]]}#!! would look like this [[https://github.com/NTDLS/TightWiki, TightWiki on GitHub]].


===Opening links in a new tab
Any link, internal or external, can specify where it opens using the !!target:!! option. The most common is !!target:blank!!, which opens the link in a new browser tab. The leading underscore is optional, so !!target:_blank!! works too. Other values are !!self!!, !!parent!! and !!top!!.

**Internal link that opens in a new tab:**
{{Card
#{[[Home, Take me home!, target:blank]]}#
}}
[[::Home, Take me home!, target:blank]]

**External link that opens in a new tab:**
{{Card
#{[[https://github.com/NTDLS/TightWiki, TightWiki on GitHub, target:blank]]}#
}}
[[https://github.com/NTDLS/TightWiki, TightWiki on GitHub, target:blank]]


===Links with Images (internal)
Links with images are created by using a comma to separate an attachment name starting with !!image:!!. In addition, you can add another comma and specify the scaling of the image as a percentage. Please note that the image has to be attached to the page.


**Link to the home page with an image:**
{{Card
#{[[Home, image:TightWiki Logo.png]]}#
}}

**Link to the home page with an image scaled to 10%**
{{Card
#{[[Home, image:TightWiki Logo.png, 10]]}#
}}

**Link to the home page using an image from another page**
{{Card
#{[[::Home, image:Builtin :: Media/TightWiki Icon 6.png, 25]]}#
}}
[[::Home, image:Builtin :: Media/TightWiki Icon 6.png, 25]]

**Link to the home page using an image from another page, opening in a new tab**
{{Card
#{[[::Home, image:Builtin :: Media/TightWiki Icon 6.png, 25, target:blank]]}#
}}
[[::Home, image:Builtin :: Media/TightWiki Icon 6.png, 25, target:blank]]

===Links with Images (external)
Links with external images (those residing on another server) are created by using a comma to separate an image URL starting with !!image:!!. External images are always shown at their original size.


**Link to the home page using an external image:**
{{Card
#{[[Home, image:http://networkdls.com/Images/Site/Home/UserSignup.gif]]}#
}}

##toc

==Overview
Basic formatting included bold, italics, underline, font-size, etc.


==Basic Formatting
Formatting is applied when special characters that dictate the format are encountered and terminated with a second occurrence of the pattern.


===Bold
**Example using #{**}# (make bold):**
{{Card
#{This is a single line where **some of the content** has been made bold.}#
}}
**Produces:**
This is a single line where **some of the content** has been made bold.


===Italics
**Example using #{//}# (make italic):**
{{Card
#{This is a single line where //some of the content// has been made italic.}#
}}
**Produces:**
This is a single line where //some of the content// has been made italic.


===Underline
**Example using #{__}# (make underline):**
{{Card
#{This is a single line where __some of the content__ has been underlined.}#
}}
**Produces:**
This is a single line where __some of the content__ has been underlined.


===Highlighted
**Example using #{!!}# (make highlighted):**
{{Card
#{This is a single line where !!some of the content!! has been highlighted.}#
}}
**Produces:**
This is a single line where !!some of the content!! has been highlighted.


===Strikethrough
**Example using #{~~}# (make strikethrough):**
{{Card
#{This is a single line where ~~some of the content~~ has been struck through.}#
}}
**Produces:**
This is a single line where ~~some of the content~~ has been struck through.


===Font Size
Using the cart symbols, you can incrementally increase the size of an entire line. The more carets you prefix the line with, the larger the text will become - up to 6.

**Example using #{^^}# (make larger):**
{{Card
#{^^This is a single line where the entire line has been made larger.}#
}}
**Produces:**
^^This is a single line where the entire line has been made larger.


**Another few examples:**
{{Card
#{^^^This is a single line where the entire line has been made larger.}#

Body:
@@HideFooterComments @@HideFooterLastModified @@protect(true)
##title @@Tags(Official-Help, Help, Wiki, Official, Standard Function)
##toc

==Overview
Namespaces are used to logically categorize pages within the wiki. Creating a namespace and placing a page in a namespace is accomplished by simply beginning the name of the page with the desired namespace name followed by two colons, followed by the desired page name.


For instance, a page with the name: **My Namespace :: My Page** would be placed in the namespace !!My Namespace!! and the page would be called !!My Page!!.


In links, glossaries, inlined searches/lists (such as [[SearchList]]), the name space is not displayed allowing for a straightforward seemless grouping of pages.

Body:
@@HideFooterComments @@HideFooterLastModified @@protect(true)
##title @@Tags(Official-Help, Help, Wiki, Official, Permission, Role, User, Account)
##toc

==Overview
User permissions are based the single assigned user role. Yes, each user can only be assigned a single role - this simplifies security. User rights are cumulative, meaning that if you are in a higher-rights role then you inherit all of the rights of all lesser roles.


A guest is defined as an anonymous user, or a user who is not logged in.


==Guest
{{Bullets
View pages.
}}


==Member
{{Bullets
All of the above permissions.
Add comments.
Delete owned comments.
}}


==Contributor
{{Bullets
All of the above permissions.
Create pages.
Edit pages.
}}

Name: Wiki Help :: StripedTable
Description: The StripedTable scope function allows you to create tables with columns and alternating colored rows.
Body:
@@HideFooterComments @@HideFooterLastModified @@protect(true)
##title @@Tags(Official-Help, Help, Wiki, Official, Scope Function)
##toc

${metaColor = #ee2401}
${keywordColor = #318000}
${identifierColor = #c6680e}
==Overview
The StripedTable scope function allows you to easily create tables with columns and alternating colored rows.

Inside of the table scope, you will simply add one line of text to create a row. Each column is created by separating your text with pipe characters (||). Cells can also be merged across columns and rows. See the examples below...


==Prototype
##Color(${keywordColor}, **#{ StripedTable }#**)(##Color(${keywordColor}, boolean) {##Color(${identifierColor}, hasBorder)}, ##Color(${keywordColor}, boolean) {##Color(${identifierColor}, isFirstRowHeader)})


===Parameters
{{Bullets
**Name:** ##Color(${identifierColor}, hasBorder) ##Color(${metaColor}, {Optional})
>**Type:** ##Color(${keywordColor}, boolean)
>**Default:** ##Color(${identifierColor}, true)
>**Description:** Whether the table will have a visible border.
**Name:** ##Color(${identifierColor}, isFirstRowHeader) ##Color(${metaColor}, {Optional})
>**Type:** ##Color(${keywordColor}, boolean)
>**Default:** ##Color(${identifierColor}, true)
>**Description:** Whether or not the first row is the header. If true, the first row will be bold and will be excluded from the alternating striped table style.
}}


==Examples
{{Code(wiki)
{{StripedTable()
Column #1 || Column #2 || Column #3 || Column #4
Row #1 || Cell #1 || Cell #2 || Cell #3
Row #2 || Cell #1 || Cell #2 || Cell #3
Row #3 || Cell #1 || Cell #2 || Cell #3
Row #4 || Cell #1 || Cell #2 || Cell #3
}}
}}

**Result:**
{{StripedTable()
Column #1 || Column #2 || Column #3 || Column #4
Row #1 || Cell #1 || Cell #2 || Cell #3
Row #2 || Cell #1 || Cell #2 || Cell #3
Row #3 || Cell #1 || Cell #2 || Cell #3
Row #4 || Cell #1 || Cell #2 || Cell #3
}}


===Merged cells
A cell containing only a less-than sign (!!<!!) is merged into the cell to its left, so that cell spans multiple columns. A cell containing only a caret (!!^!!) is merged into the cell above it, so that cell spans multiple rows. The two can be combined to merge a block of cells.

{{Bullets
Merged cells must form a rectangle.
Cells in the body can not be merged into the header row.
To display a lone !!<!! or !!^!! in a cell, wrap it in literal markup (see [[Literals]]).
}}

{{Code(wiki)
{{StripedTable()
Feature || Free || Pro || Enterprise
Sync || Yes || < || <
Export || No || Yes || <
Audit logs || ^ || ^ || ^
}}
}}

**Result:**
{{StripedTable()
Feature || Free || Pro || Enterprise
Sync || Yes || < || <
Export || No || Yes || <
Audit logs || ^ || ^ || ^
}}

In this example the first "Yes" spans all three plan columns, "No" spans two rows and the second "Yes" spans two columns and two rows.

==Overview
The TOC standard function displays a table of contents based on the head tags in the page. Each heading will be linked to the header anchors to allow skipping directly to a given section. By default. the table of contents is built in the order that the page headings are found thereby creating a reasonable document outline. However, you can override this behavior by passing true to the alphabetized parameter. When alphabetized, the table retains the basic hierarchy, but the members are order alphabetically.

Name: Wiki Help :: Whitespace
Description: How the wiki handles whitespace and what you can do to manipulate it.
Body:
@@HideFooterComments @@HideFooterLastModified @@protect(true)
##title @@Tags(Official-Help, Help, Wiki, Official)
##toc

==Overview
Whitespace and HTML have a troubled past and TightWiki tries its best to be intuitive with both maintaining whitespace and minimizing excess whitespace.


Any new-lines/empty-lines you leave in a page source will be converted to a HTML line-break. However, when this will lead to more than one line-break being inserted. the engine will collapse half of them. This allows you to put spacing in the source to make it readable while controlling the resulting page body.


==Functions
A few functions exist to help you add whitespace.
